newsitem.title: UK: LME metals end scattered, copper and zinc strong.
newsitem.headline: LME metals end scattered, copper and zinc strong.

text.p: LME metals each went their own way on Friday afternoon, with copper, nickel and zinc putting in strong performances but the others weak or lacklustre ahead of Third Wednesday pricing next week.
Three months copper reversed in the afternoon and re-attacked the psychological $2,600 per tonne mark, before ending the afternoon kerb $10 higher at $2,590.

The market started the morning by looking at the downside, hitting a low of $2,572, but ratcheted higher the rest of the day. It hit a high of $2,604 in the second afternoon ring and ran into profit-taking.

In the short-term the market was overbought, with the 14-day RSI at 77 percent. "The technical indicators are screaming overbought. At best, it will manage to move sideways on Monday," one trader said.
The market streaked up to $2,609 on Thursday on a burst of options covering against a backdrop of tightness and supply disruptions.
News that energy problems at Russia's Norilsk was cutting output gave the market another fillip, traders said.
A strike at Inco in Canada would deprive the market of 9,000 tonnes of supply each month, analyst Larry Kaplan of Flemings Global Mining Group said.
Heavy rains and landslides have hit northern Chile, but Codelco said operations at its Salvador copper mine were normal.
Despite all the bullish news, some analysts were wary of reports China may be tempted to sell at these high levels.
LME copper inventories fell by 6,975 tonnes this week, but Rudolf Wolff analyst Martin Squires said the market should keep a close eye on stocks for signs of a possible turnaround in fundamentals.
Nickel also bounced off its lows, bottoming out at $7,140 before the market digested news of the Norilsk difficulties.
It ended up $145 at $7,340, off its high of $7,390.
"It's a good close, but it would have been better above $7,350 since its failed here several times before," a trader said.
Zinc also showed resilience, as the bulls won a battle in the morning when good two-way business was seen between $1,353 and $1,356.
After it broke loose, prices flew up within $1 of the previous $1,375 peak hit on June 5.
They ended $15 stronger at $1,374.
Aluminium extended losses after heavy cash selling in the morning rattled the market, a trader said. Three months shed $29 to $1,586.
"I would expect people to be sellers on Monday, it's not looking good," he added.
Next support is pegged at $1,575, then $1,540.
Tin slid to the bottom of its recent range, breaching a modest uptrend seen the past few days.
It ended down $30 at $5,580, a support level it has hit four times since May 29.
Below there, the support was pegged at $5,510, the low of June 2.
One trader said the market was looking terrible and falls to $5,400 or even $5,300 were possible.
Lead was down $6 at $629, after failing on a lacklustre attempt to break the 30-day moving average a few dollars higher.
Alloy ended at slightly weaker at $1,475/80.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
